title: AI-heavy workflows penalize private meetings and stale documents, forcing human decisions into observable channels
text: When decisions occur in unlogged in-person meetings or private direct messages, autonomous agents lack the context needed to update their goals and assumptions. Conversely, stale documentation actively misroutes agents—such as a months-old document about company swag that caused agents to keep routing mug and t-shirt requests to an employee long after their responsibilities had changed. To feed agents accurate context, standing instruction files grew from a few hundred in July 2025 to 8,500 a year later, while agents appeared in nearly half of public Slack channels as per-employee sub-teams without reducing human-to-human thread density.
qualification: Internal Slack communication network analysis, telemetry, and interviews at Anthropic; high transparency requires cultural norms where leaders defend feedback openly.

public_locator.value: Private work, in unlogged meetings and direct messages, is invisible, confusing and discouraged in an AI-heavy workplace. ... The need to feed AI context requires observability of human work and decisions.
